title: Workflows, agents, and who owns the control flow

items.stem: Which difference is what separates a workflow from an agent?

options.text: Model size: larger models run agents and smaller ones run workflows
Tool use: systems that call any tool are agents, the rest are workflows
Who picks the next step: the model in an agent, the code in a workflow
Timing: agents answer while a user waits and workflows run in the background

items.stem: In your makerspace assistant, the code always runs search_manuals on the student's question, then calls the model once with the pages it found to write the answer, then stops. Which description fits?

options.text: A workflow: the code fixes the steps, though a tool and a model are used
An agent: it combines a tool and a model to answer the student's question
An agent: the model chooses its own wording, so the model controls the flow
Neither: a system that uses a tool and a model must run as a loop

items.stem: A student submits the booking form, which already gives the machine and the time. The program's code calls check_calendar, sees the slot is free, calls book_slot, and then calls the model once to write a friendly confirmation message. The model is not used for anything else. How many times is the model called for this request?

Every booking request follows the same steps in the same order: check the calendar, book the slot if it is free (otherwise stop and say so), then send a confirmation. Which design is better for this part of the assistant, and why?

options.text: An agent, because agent designs are the more capable and modern choice
A fixed workflow, because the steps are known and code runs them identically
An agent, because a model choosing each step is safer than fixed code
A fixed workflow, because workflows never call a model and so cost nothing

items.stem: Your sponsor's model budget is small. In one or two sentences, why does a fixed workflow usually cost less per request than an agent doing the same task?
In one sentence, what is true of a task that makes an agent a better fit than a fixed workflow?
